title: ¿Por qué tu estómago no se digiere a sí mismo? 🫃
staging_mode_proposal: cutaway: the sealed digestive system in x-ray, then a section through the stomach wall showing its layers, the mucus gel and the acid.
curiosity_reason: Everyone knows the stomach is full of acid; hidden.
hook_question: ¿Por qué tu estómago no se digiere a sí mismo?
false_belief: El ácido del estómago es débil, por eso no lo daña.

description:
¿Por qué tu estómago no se digiere a sí mismo? Porque una capa de moco con bicarbonato frena el ácido antes de tocar la pared.
Y lo que se daña, se renueva cada pocos días. 🫃
Envíaselo a ese amigo que se come cualquier cosa sin pensarlo dos veces.

scenes.name: hook
scenes.narration: ¿Por qué tu estómago no se digiere a sí mismo? Mucha gente cree que el ácido del estómago es débil, y por eso no lo daña.
scenes.what_changes: The digestive system in x-ray on the stage; a bite of food slides down the oesophagus and drops into the stomach, which glows with acid; the tag ¿ÁCIDO DÉBIL? hangs on it.
scenes.transformation: estómago vacío → cae un bocado al ácido
scenes.camera: bajada siguiendo el bocado por el esófago hasta el estómago

elements.name: a human stomach in an x-ray digestive system
elements.risk: low: sealed asset; the x-ray state is its brief

scenes.name: acido
scenes.narration: Al contrario: fabrica ácido clorhídrico, tan fuerte que, junto con sus enzimas, deshace la carne que comes.
scenes.what_changes: Inside the stomach, a piece of meat sinks into a pool of glowing acid; its surface frays and comes apart into strands and then a cloud.
scenes.transformation: trozo de carne entero → se deshace en el ácido
scenes.camera: empuje dentro del estómago hasta el trozo de carne

elements.name: a piece of meat dissolving in stomach acid
elements.route: build: meat chunk (material route, stylised, no real texture) inside the stomach section; acid as an emissive liquid

scenes.name: moco
scenes.narration: Y la pared del estómago también es carne. Lo que la salva es una capa de moco espeso que la cubre por dentro.
scenes.what_changes: Push-through into the wall: a section of the stomach wall in layers, and on its inner face a thick translucent gel spreads out and covers it, between the acid and the cells.
scenes.transformation: pared desnuda frente al ácido → una capa de moco la cubre
scenes.camera: travelling a través de la pared, del ácido a las capas

elements.name: a cross-section of the stomach wall with a mucus layer
elements.route: build: layered wall section (muscle, cell row, gel), stylised, attached to the digestive-system stomach
elements.risk: high: a layer stack reads as a 'cake' unless the stomach is in frame; proof P2

scenes.name: bicarbonato
scenes.narration: Ese moco atrapa bicarbonato, que neutraliza el ácido justo antes de que toque las células.
scenes.what_changes: Acid droplets fall into the gel; as they sink they meet bicarbonate beads, fizz and change from the acid colour to neutral before reaching the cell row.
scenes.transformation: gotas de ácido → se apagan dentro del moco antes de la pared
scenes.camera: seguimiento de una gota de ácido hundiéndose en el moco

elements.name: acid drops neutralised inside a mucus layer
elements.route: same section as P2; drops as emissive spheres with a colour change and fizz
elements.risk: high: event element, read with the P2 section

scenes.name: renueva
scenes.narration: Aun así, algo de ácido pasa y daña las células de la superficie. Por eso se renuevan cada pocos días, antes de que el daño avance.
scenes.what_changes: The turn: a few drops get through; cells on the surface darken, crack and peel away; new cells push up from below and take their place, row after row, and the gel closes over them again.
scenes.transformation: células dañadas → se desprenden y otras nuevas ocupan su lugar
scenes.camera: empuje a la fila de células y retroceso cuando suben las nuevas
overlays_plan: mark red on the damaged cells at 'daña'

elements.name: damaged cells peeling off a stomach lining as new ones grow
elements.route: same section as P2; cells as rounded blocks, peel and rise animation

scenes.name: cierre
scenes.narration: Así que tu estómago sí se ataca a sí mismo: solo que se repara más rápido de lo que se daña. Envíaselo a ese amigo que se come cualquier cosa sin pensarlo dos veces.
scenes.what_changes: Single reframe image: back out to the whole stomach in x-ray, its inner lining lit in the accent and renewing in waves while the acid churns inside.
scenes.transformation: corte de la pared → el estómago entero renovando su revestimiento
scenes.camera: retroceso desde la pared hasta el sistema digestivo completo

sources: Stomach acid is hydrochloric acid secreted by parietal cells; with pepsin it digests protein (meat): standard physiology; TeachMePhysiology 'Mucus production' and 'Gastric acid' (live search 2026-11-11). FLAGGED: add a textbook or Britannica reference at the beat sheet. No pH value is spoken.

Protection: surface (foveolar) cells secrete a thick mucus gel; bicarbonate trapped in it keeps the cell surface near neutral while the lumen is strongly acidic; tight junctions between cells: TeachMePhysiology 'Mucus production'; IFLScience 'Your stomach juices are so acidic they can digest zinc and meat, so why don't they digest you?' (live search 2026-11-11).

Renewal: the surface lining is replaced every few days (commonly given as 3-5 days). FLAGGED: only secondary sources were found on 2026-11-11; read a physiology source at the beat sheet. Spoken as 'cada pocos días', no number.
When the barrier fails the acid damages the wall (peptic ulcer): TeachMePhysiology. Not spoken as a medical claim; the script makes no health advice.
No number is spoken or rendered in this script.
simplifications: The wall section is enlarged and reduced to a few layers; the mucus is drawn as a uniform gel and bicarbonate as beads.
Cell renewal is shown as a row replaced in seconds; it takes days.
flatness_test: 1. hook: a bite drops into the stomach's acid.
2. acido: a piece of meat comes apart in the acid.
3. moco: the wall in section; a thick gel spreads over its inner face.
4. bicarbonato: acid drops fizz and turn neutral inside the gel.
5. renueva: damaged surface cells peel off and new ones push up (turn).
6. cierre: the whole stomach, its lining renewing in waves.
